title: I just wanted to try this AI thing man and things kind of got out of hand
author: aimhelix
selftext:
I'm not a dev by any means, but I'm a CD/AD in advertising so I know the design apps and some 3D in my past life. A while ago I tried Claude to make a game, a Pearl Harbor game to be precise and the result was the most disappointing output I ever played I didn't bother touching it again lol. I'm not a coder by any means. At most, I can code HTML/CSS (designer stuff) and some C++ for my Arduino / microcontroller hobby. Things I consider 'easy' programming. But the maths behind game programming has always turned me off.

This time I came in with a clear approach. Spent nearly a week planning.. maybe not, but almost a week before any code was written or assets made. I poked holes on my idea, ran simulations based on the plan to make it as solid as possible and then finally I pulled the trigger on making the first 'gray box' - a term I learned in this process.

Claude insisted that I work on making this part good. Ignore the boxes. There's one thing he said that stood out to me that I will never forget that I thought I should share:

"If your gray boxes aren't fun to shoot, no artwork will save your game." 

Holy shit he's right. I tuned it as best as I could. I laid down the timing so that I directed everything from the pace of the reload to the the pace of the battles. I followed our planning milestones tightly. But as a visual person, I insisted that I be allowed to break the rules early and inject soundfx and impactfx. My reasoning being I'll be beta testing this 1000's of times.. I'll need some treat to keep me coming back and Claude agreed.

So little by little I chopped away at my little game. I'd go into blender and work on my models, optimize the texture.. I'm a big gamer so I sort of knew what "shaders" and "culling" and things like that are, but not precisely but with some guidance I think it didn't turn out too bad.

I realized then than my game is turning out to be ARMA that will run on mobile phones lol. I did as much optimization as I could. Minimizing triangle counts on my models. Faking foliage with cards, etc. and baking normals into low poly things like that WIP sandbag by the pit.

Anyway. Here's where I'm at. Still in the process of optimizing and now trying to tighten up the sound design on the FX work I did. 

I've made tools now that make it easy for me to go through game asset that tell me when/if it was ever modified/enhanced, etc. so I can keep a tab on what needs my art direction.

In the meantime I've started several pipelines that hand off things at the end of each tasks (ex. after art, code ads it and then QA checks it against my guardrails). I think I'm doing this right? LOL. But again, I am trying to learn this along the way and it has got me hooked.
